laws.rule: Recreational cannabis is illegal in Texas; only low-THC cannabis under the Compassionate Use Program is allowed, for registered patients. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law, including on federal land such as national parks.

sources.title: Cannabis and the law: recreational use
sources.supports: recreational use illegal (read via a search-index snapshot)

items.text: Possessing a usable quantity of marihuana is an offence: two ounces or less is a Class B misdemeanour, more than two and up to four ounces a Class A misdemeanour (Health and Safety Code s. 481.121).
Only low-THC cannabis is available, on a Texas prescription from a licensed dispensing organisation, and smoking it is prohibited (Occupations Code s. 169.001).

layers.authority: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
layers.process: The park limits visitors on weekends and holidays and closes to people without reservations once it reaches capacity. A day pass can be reserved up to 30 days ahead through the state reservation system or by phone on (512) 389-8900. The entrance fee is US$8 (about A$11.40) per person aged 13 and over; children 12 and under are free. Check the date before paying: the park may not honour a pass with the wrong date in busy periods. Backcountry area permits are picked up at headquarters. Rock climbers must check in at headquarters. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Big Bend National Park
layers.process: A backcountry permit is required for all backcountry camping, including backpacking and primitive roadside campsites; river trips need a permit too (day-use river and stock permits are free). Permits are issued in person at Panther Junction Visitor Center, available 24 hours before the first night; some primitive roadside sites can be reserved on Recreation.gov up to 180 days ahead. The park page says river permits can be had in person up to 7 days ahead, and that Chisos Mountains backcountry sites are issued in person from 1 May to 31 October. A permit costs US$10 per night (about A$14.20). Permits cover up to 14 consecutive nights; groups are limited to 15 people. The page notes that after heavy rain and road closures some campsites could only be obtained in person; confirm the current position with the park. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
